title: Iman and the Unlit Room
logline: Iman descends into Hayat and learns the dark was only unremembered light.
story: Everyone warned that Hayat, who was abundant life, could not be reached — the way down was made of everything Iman had refused to remember. Iman, who carried faith, went looking anyway. So instead of fighting the dark, Iman sat in it and listened — and the dark, for the first time, was not afraid of being seen. When Iman rose, nothing outside had changed, and everything had. The darkness had not been an enemy; it was only a room with the light switched off, waiting for someone unhurried enough to find the switch within.
moral: The darkness is not the absence of light, but light that has not yet been remembered.
attribution: a Pagarek parable, from Project Genesis
